questions.question_text:
A gas bottle is weighed as $42$ kg.
Find the percentage error of this measurement, correct to two decimal places.

options.why: Used the precision of $1$ kg as the absolute error instead of halving it.
Forgot to multiply by $100\%$, leaving the decimal $0.0119...$ rounded to two places.
Halved the absolute error a second time, using $0.25$ kg instead of $0.5$ kg.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Precision} = 1$ kg, so the absolute error is $0.5$ kg.
$\dfrac{0.5}{42} \times 100\%$
$= 1.1904...\%$
$\approx 1.19\%$

questions.question_text:
A book's spine is measured as $36.5$ cm long.
Find the percentage error of this measurement, correct to two decimal places.

options.why: Used the precision of $0.1$ cm as the absolute error instead of halving it.
Treated the precision as $1$ cm, ignoring the decimal place, giving an absolute error of $0.5$ cm.
Assumed the measurement was to the nearest $0.5$ cm, giving an absolute error of $0.25$ cm.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Precision} = 0.1$ cm, so the absolute error is $0.05$ cm.
$\dfrac{0.05}{36.5} \times 100\%$
$= 0.1369...\%$
$\approx 0.14\%$

questions.question_text: A street is measured as $380$ m long, to the nearest $10$ m. Find the percentage error of this measurement, correct to two decimal places.

options.why: Used the precision of $10$ m as the absolute error instead of halving it.
Ignored the 'nearest $10$ m' and used an absolute error of $0.5$ m.
Halved the absolute error a second time, using $2.5$ m instead of $5$ m.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Precision} = 10$ m, so the absolute error is $5$ m.
$\dfrac{5}{380} \times 100\%$
$= 1.3157...\%$
$\approx 1.32\%$

questions.question_text:
A saucepan holds $2.75$ L, correct to the nearest $10$ mL.
Find the percentage error of this measurement, correct to two decimal places.

options.why: Divided $5$ mL by $2.75$ without converting the litres to millilitres.
Used the precision of $10$ mL as the absolute error instead of halving it.
Halved the absolute error a second time, using $2.5$ mL instead of $5$ mL.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Precision} = 10$ mL, so the absolute error is $5$ mL.
$2.75$ L $= 2750$ mL
$\dfrac{5}{2750} \times 100\%$
$= 0.1818...\%$
$\approx 0.18\%$

questions.question_text:
A shelf is measured as $1.8$ m with one tape and $1.84$ m with a more precise tape.
Which measurement has the smaller percentage error, and why?

options.text: $1.84$ m, because its absolute error is ten times smaller while the measurement is about the same size.
$1.8$ m, because a shorter decimal is a rounder, more reliable value.
options.why: Fewer decimal places means a larger precision and a larger absolute error, not a more reliable measurement.

options.text: Neither — both percentage errors are equal because they measure the same shelf.
options.why: Percentage error depends on the instrument's precision, not on the object being measured.

options.text: $1.84$ m, because a larger measurement always gives a smaller percentage error.
options.why: The measurements differ by only $0.04$ m; the smaller percentage error comes from the smaller absolute error, not the larger value.

questions.solution_text:
$1.8$ m: absolute error $= 0.05$ m
$\dfrac{0.05}{1.8} \times 100\% \approx 2.78\%$
$1.84$ m: absolute error $= 0.005$ m
$\dfrac{0.005}{1.84} \times 100\% \approx 0.27\%$
The measurements are nearly equal, so the ten-times-smaller absolute error of $1.84$ m gives the smaller percentage error.

questions.question_text: A packet of flour is weighed as $220$ g, to the nearest $5$ g. Find the percentage error of this measurement, correct to two decimal places.

options.why: Used the precision of $5$ g as the absolute error instead of halving it.
Ignored the 'nearest $5$ g' and used an absolute error of $0.5$ g.
Used $10$ g as the absolute error, doubling the precision instead of halving it.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Precision} = 5$ g, so the absolute error is $2.5$ g.
$\dfrac{2.5}{220} \times 100\%$
$= 1.1363...\%$
$\approx 1.14\%$

questions.question_text:
A cable is measured as $15$ m long with a percentage error of $2\%$.
What is the absolute error of this measurement?

options.why: Read the $2\%$ itself as the absolute error in metres.
Divided the measurement by $2$ instead of finding $2\%$ of it.
Halved the absolute error again after finding $2\%$ of $15$ m.

questions.question_text:
A tile is measured as $5.0$ cm wide, correct to one decimal place.
Find the percentage error of this measurement, correct to two decimal places.

options.why: Ignored the trailing zero and treated the precision as $1$ cm instead of $0.1$ cm.
Used the precision of $0.1$ cm as the absolute error instead of halving it.
Forgot to multiply by $100\%$, leaving the decimal $0.01$.

questions.solution_text:
The trailing zero shows the precision is $0.1$ cm, so the absolute error is $0.05$ cm.
$\dfrac{0.05}{5} \times 100\%$
$= 1\%$
$= 1.00\%$
